name: application-pto-balance-card
title: PTO Balance Card
description: PTO balance card with a remaining-days readout, a usage progress bar, and an accrued/used/pending stat row computed from real numeric inputs.
useWhen: Showing an employee's paid-time-off balance in an HR dashboard or self-service portal.
You want accrued/used/pending figures and the derived remaining balance to always agree, computed from the same source numbers.
A direct "Request time off" action belongs right next to the balance it affects.
avoidWhen: You're showing a subscription/billing plan, not leave balance — use `plan-and-billing-card` for that unrelated billing context.
There's no request flow — drop the action button and show the balance as a read-only summary.
The organization tracks leave in hours rather than days — adjust the unit throughout rather than hardcoding "days".
responsiveBehavior: Single-column card; the three-stat row stays in a fixed 3-column grid at any card width, wrapping text rather than columns.
accessibility: Remaining days is computed (accrued − used − pending) rather than hardcoded, so it can never drift out of sync with the stat row below it.
The progress bar's fill percentage is derived from the same real numbers as the stat row, not an independent hardcoded value.
Accrued/Used/Pending use a <dl> so each figure has a programmatic label, not just visual proximity to its heading.
Pending days are colored distinctly (amber) from confirmed used days, signaling their provisional status through both color and the "Pending" label text.

variants.title: PTO Balance Card
variants.description: 15 accrued days, 6 used, 2 pending, 9 remaining, with a usage progress bar and a request button.
accessibility: All displayed figures (remaining, progress bar width) are derived from the same accrued/used/pending inputs, eliminating drift.

variants.title: PTO Balance Card (Dark)
variants.description: PTO balance card adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Progress bar and pending-stat colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
